papers.title: A transcriptomics-based computational drug repurposing pipeline identifies simvastatin and primaquine as therapeutics for endometriosis.
papers.abstract: Endometriosis has limited treatment options, prompting the search for data-driven therapeutics. We previously used a transcriptomics-based computational drug repositioning pipeline and identified several drug candidates. Fenoprofen, our top in silico candidate, was validated in a rat model of endometriosis-associated pain. Building on this, we evaluated two additional candidates, simvastatin and primaquine. Using the rat model, we conducted behavioral testing, bulk RNA sequencing, and differential expression analysis to assess their therapeutic potential. We also assessed endometriosis diagnos
papers.summary: This study applies a transcriptomics-based computational drug repurposing pipeline to identify simvastatin and primaquine as potential therapeutics for endometriosis, building on prior validation of fenoprofen. Using a rat model, the authors performed behavioral testing and bulk RNA sequencing to evaluate the candidates' efficacy, suggesting these drugs may offer new treatment options for endometriosis.

papers.title: Decoding cancer with artificial intelligence: Transforming research, diagnosis, and therapy with future insights.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading global health burdens, with increasing complexity in genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets presenting significant challenges for effective management. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a powerful tool to address these challenges by enabling pattern recognition, knowledge integration, and data-driven decision-making. This review highlights recent advances in the application of AI across cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy. In research, AI accelerates drug discovery and repurposing, enhances genomic data interpretation, and facilitates biomarker
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence is transforming cancer research, diagnosis, and therapy by enabling pattern recognition and data-driven decision-making across complex genomic, imaging, and clinical datasets. It highlights AI's role in accelerating drug discovery, improving genomic interpretation, and facilitating biomarker identification, offering a comprehensive overview of current advances and future directions.

papers.title: New thinking for the next generation of antimalarials.
papers.abstract: Despite decades of intensive research and substantial clinical gains, malaria remains a major global health challenge exacerbated by the continued emergence of drug-resistant strains of the causative agent, Plasmodium parasites. Encouragingly, recent advances in functional genomics, chemical biology and computational science are reshaping antimalarial drug discovery. In this review, we examine the discovery and development of next-generation antimalarials, including advances in phenotypic and target-based screening, omics-enabled target discovery and emerging therapeutic modalities such as lon
papers.summary: This review discusses how recent advances in functional genomics, chemical biology, and computational science are transforming antimalarial drug discovery. It highlights new approaches like phenotypic and target-based screening, omics-enabled target identification, and emerging therapeutic modalities to combat drug-resistant malaria.

papers.title: Discovery of novel acridine based inhibitors of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) via pharmacophore modeling and machine learning-driven virtual screening followed by molecular dynamic studies.
papers.abstract: Bruton's Tyrosine Kinase (BTK) has been recently recognized as an important drug design target for treating B-cell malignancies. Unfortunately, drug resistance is making the treatment of B-cell malignancies challenging. In this study, we employed a dual machine learning drug design approach that involves two parallel branches: the QSAR-GFA modeling (Branch 1) which engages the development of an interpretable structure activity relationships, and the KNIME® based machine learning modeling (Branch 2) which aimed at achieving high predictive accuracy. Subsequently, six machine learning modules, e
papers.summary: This study presents a dual machine-learning approach combining QSAR-GFA and KNIME-based models to discover novel acridine-based inhibitors of Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK), a key target for B-cell malignancies. The workflow integrates pharmacophore modeling, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify promising lead compounds with potential to overcome drug resistance.

papers.title: Correction to: Structure-informed machine learning for drug discovery: a task-centric perspective.
papers.summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article in Briefings in Bioinformatics. It does not contain new scientific findings or data.

papers.title: Synthesis, X-ray structures and biological evaluation of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives as anti-inflammatory and antioxidant agents: an integrated in vitro and in silico study.
papers.abstract: In the field of medicinal chemistry, the design of small molecules is acknowledged as an effective strategy. This study may contribute to the global fight against inflammatory diseases by focusing on the synthesis of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives incorporating para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and benzocaine moieties and evaluating their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. Compounds 1a-1i, 2a-2g and 3a-3f were efficiently prepared via a one-pot Kabachnik-Fields reaction in moderate to high yields. Structural characterization was achieved using spectroscopic techniques and single-c
papers.summary: This study describes the synthesis of novel α-aminophosphonate derivatives containing para-aminobenzoic acid and benzocaine moieties via a one-pot Kabachnik-Fields reaction, followed by structural characterization including X-ray crystallography. The compounds were evaluated for anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities using in vitro assays and in silico studies, identifying promising leads for further development.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Antibacterial Activity of Moroccan Monofloral Honeys Against Multidrug-Resistant Uropathogens: In Vitro, ADMET, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Approaches.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections represent a significant public health issue exacerbated by bacterial antibiotic resistance. Honey, due to its phenolic compounds, offers a promising natural alternative. This study explores the phenolic profile of monofloral honeys from the Beni Mellal-Khenifra region and their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant strains. Four monofloral honeys from Beni Mellal-Khenifra were analyzed for their phenolic composition and evaluated for antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogenic bacteria. Computational studies were also performed to expl
papers.summary: This study profiles the phenolic compounds in four Moroccan monofloral honeys and tests their antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant uropathogenic bacteria, finding promising inhibitory effects. Computational analyses (ADMET, molecular docking, and dynamics) suggest that specific phenolic compounds may be responsible for the antibacterial action, supporting honey as a potential natural alternative for treating resistant urinary tract infections.

papers.title: Quinoline and Phthalimide Substituted Silicon Phthalocyanines as Multi-Target Inhibitors of Cholinesterases and Carbonic Anhydrases.
papers.abstract: Two novel axially substituted silicon phthalocyanines bearing 5,7-dichloro-8-hydroxy-2-methylquinoline (1a) and N-(hydroxymethyl)phthalimide (2a) moieties were synthesized and characterized by UV-Vis, FT-IR, 1H NMR, and mass spectrometry techniques. The biological potential of the synthesized compounds was evaluated through in vitro inhibition studies against acetylcholinesterase (AChE), butyrylcholinesterase (BChE), and human carbonic anhydrase isoenzymes I and II (hCA I and hCA II). IC50 values were determined as 91.28 ± 25.21, 43.31 ± 20.35, 8.50 ± 2.80 and 23.35 ± 12.98 µM, for compound 1a
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study reports the synthesis and characterization of two novel silicon phthalocyanines substituted with quinoline and phthalimide groups, and evaluates their inhibitory activity against cholinesterases and carbonic anhydrases. The compounds showed moderate inhibition, with IC50 values in the micromolar range, suggesting potential as multi-target enzyme inhibitors for therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Integrated In Silico Discovery of Thymoquinone Analogs Targeting the Keap1-Nrf2 Pathway for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Therapy.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress drives neuronal vulnerability in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), making the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway a vital therapeutic target. While thymoquinone (TQ) modulates this axis, its efficacy is limited by low potency and poor drug-likeness. We utilized an integrated in silico workflow-including validated QSAR modeling (R2 = 0.68, Q2 ext = 0.66), ADMET profiling, docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics, and MM-PBSA analysis-to identify improved TQ-derived Keap1 inhibitors. Screening 64 analogs prioritized three leads (CHEMBL3416163, CHEMBL4636830, and CHEMBL221598) with favorable safety
papers.summary: This study used a computational pipeline combining QSAR modeling, ADMET prediction, docking, and molecular dynamics to identify three thymoquinone analogs that may better inhibit the Keap1-Nrf2 pathway, a key oxidative stress response target in ALS. The lead compounds showed improved predicted potency and safety profiles compared to thymoquinone, offering promising candidates for further experimental validation.

papers.title: Inhibition and Molecular Recognition of Lactoperoxidase by Acetohydrazide-Based Sulfonamide Derivatives.
papers.abstract: Lactoperoxidase (LPO) is a heme-containing enzyme widely distributed in mammalian secretions, contributing to host defense through the generation of antimicrobial oxidants. Unintended inhibition of LPO by therapeutic agents may impair mucosal immunity, making the investigation of potential inhibitors clinically relevant. In this study, the inhibitory effects of 11 acetohydrazide-based sulfonamide derivatives on bovine milk LPO were investigated using combined biochemical and computational approaches. The compounds exhibited diverse inhibition profiles, with IC50 values ranging from 2.32 ± 0.14
papers.summary: This study investigates the inhibitory effects of 11 acetohydrazide-based sulfonamide derivatives on lactoperoxidase (LPO), a key enzyme in mucosal immunity. Using biochemical assays and computational methods, the authors found that these compounds inhibit LPO with varying potency (IC50 values as low as 2.32 µM), which may have clinical implications for drug safety.

papers.title: Machine learning of sunitinib resistance genes reveals that SP5 regulates angiogenesis and sunitinib resistance in RCC via the VEGFA/AKT axis.
papers.abstract: Sunitinib resistance remains a major clinical challenge in renal cell carcinoma, and the underlying molecular mechanisms are incompletely understood. SP5, a member of the specificity protein transcription factor family, has been implicated in tumor progression, but its role in sunitinib resistance and angiogenesis in RCC is unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify genes associated with sunitinib resistance in renal cell carcinoma (RCC), revealing that the transcription factor SP5 promotes angiogenesis and sunitinib resistance through the VEGFA/AKT signaling axis. The findings suggest SP5 as a potential therapeutic target to overcome sunitinib resistance in RCC.

papers.title: A cross-species drug-discovery platform to accelerate the identification of lifespan-extending interventions.
papers.abstract: We develop an integrated, high-throughput platform to evaluate pharmacological lifespan-extending interventions across five model organisms spanning unicellular to mammalian biology including yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, killifish, and mice. By combining automated imaging, miniaturized assays, and deep-learning-based death detection, we evaluate over 400 compounds across thousands of conditions. In S. cerevisiae, a miniaturized PI/flow cytometry CLS assay enables scalable screening and identifies key assay confounders, while in C. elegans and D. melanogaster, compact imaging platforms couple
papers.summary: This paper presents a high-throughput, cross-species drug-discovery platform that tests lifespan-extending compounds across five model organisms (yeast, nematodes, flies, killifish, and mice). By integrating automated imaging, miniaturized assays, and deep-learning-based death detection, the platform screened over 400 compounds and identified key assay confounders, accelerating the discovery of aging interventions.

papers.title: Olfactory proteomics reveals the capacity of the HDAC1 inhibitor pyroxamide to halt the α-synuclein preformed fibrils-induced damage in nasal epithelial, microglial and dopaminergic neuronal cell lines.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder mainly characterized by the degeneration of dopaminergic neurons originating in the substantia nigra (SN) pars compacta and projecting to other brain regions, giving rise to motor and non-motor symptoms. Despite significant progress in understanding the molecular and cellular disruptions associated with PD, there remains an unmet clinical need for effective therapies. In this study, proteomic analysis of the olfactory tract (OT) in controls with no known neurological history (n = 17) and PD subjects (n = 21) revealed
papers.summary: This study uses proteomic analysis of the olfactory tract from Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and controls to identify disease-related changes, and then tests the HDAC1 inhibitor pyroxamide in cell models. The findings suggest that pyroxamide can protect nasal epithelial, microglial, and dopaminergic neuronal cells from damage induced by α-synuclein preformed fibrils, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic for PD.

papers.title: Predicting Single-Cell Perturbation Responses Across Biological Contexts With a Deep Generative Model Integrating Optimal Transport.
papers.abstract: Predicting how single cells respond to perturbations is a central problem in computational biology, with potential relevance to emerging artificial intelligence virtual cell (AIVC) research and drug-discovery efforts. However, substantial variation in perturbation responses across biological contexts and the limited generalizability of current models make prediction across cell types, patients, species, and other contexts particularly challenging. To address this challenge, we present single-cell perturbation inference via latent optimal transport (scPILOT), a query-conditioned framework for t
papers.summary: This paper introduces scPILOT, a deep generative model that uses optimal transport to predict single-cell perturbation responses across different biological contexts, such as cell types and species. The model addresses the challenge of generalizing predictions to unseen contexts, which is important for applications in drug discovery and the development of AI virtual cells.

papers.title: Molecular insights and ADMET profiling of iridoids as candidate leads for erectile dysfunction therapy.
papers.abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) significantly affects male psychosocial health and has an increasing incidence. Although phosphodiesterase 5 (PDEi-5) inhibitors are the first-line therapy, the occurrence of visual side effects resulting from cross-inhibition of the PDE-6 isoform limits their adoption. In this context, the plant Veronica anagallis-aquatica L. emerges as a promising source of bioactive therapeutic compounds. This work investigated the inhibitory potential and selectivity of eight iridoid glycosides from this species against PDE-5 and PDE-6. The results identified catalposide as the mo
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluated eight iridoid glycosides from Veronica anagallis-aquatica as potential PDE5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction, identifying catalposide as a promising lead with selectivity over PDE6, which may reduce visual side effects. The work combines molecular docking and ADMET profiling to support further development of this natural product as a safer alternative to current PDE5 inhibitors.

papers.title: Bridging the AI Divide in Drug Discovery: Practical Lessons from Capacity Strengthening in Africa.
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become an integral part of drug discovery in high-income countries. However, these advances have yet to be broadly adopted by research ecosystems in many low- and middle-income countries in Africa, where understudied infectious diseases, compounded by a growing noncommunicable disease burden, cause millions of deaths each year. Given adequate support and appropriate models AI could play a transformative role in under-resourced biomedical research ecosystems in Africa, democratizing drug discovery research. There is an urgent need to invest in building the criti
papers.summary: This perspective highlights the gap in AI adoption for drug discovery between high-income countries and African research ecosystems, where infectious and noncommunicable diseases cause millions of deaths. The authors argue that with adequate support and appropriate models, AI could democratize drug discovery in under-resourced settings, and they call for urgent investment in capacity strengthening.

papers.title: Accelerate Your Science: Direct-to-Biology Strategies in Medicinal Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Direct-to-biology (D2B) is a powerful strategy that accelerates early drug discovery. It enables compounds to be synthesized in miniaturized formats and evaluated directly as crude reaction mixtures. This bypasses the need for purification during the initial design-make-test cycle. Advances in robust synthetic methodologies, automation, reaction miniaturization, and biological screening have transformed D2B from a proof-of-concept approach into a versatile medicinal chemistry platform. This platform is applicable to fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, proteolysis-targeting ch
papers.summary: This review discusses the direct-to-biology (D2B) strategy in medicinal chemistry, which accelerates early drug discovery by synthesizing compounds in miniaturized formats and testing them directly as crude reaction mixtures, bypassing purification. The authors highlight recent advances in synthetic methods, automation, and biological screening that have made D2B a versatile platform for applications such as fragment optimization, covalent ligands, macrocycles, and proteolysis-targeting chimeras.

papers.title: Medicinal and Crop Protection Chemistry: Breaking Barriers, Building Synergies.
papers.abstract: Recognizing the strong interconnection between human, animal, and environmental health, the "One Health" perspective listed by WHO promotes cross-disciplinary integration as a key strategy to address global challenges. Within this framework, this perspective article summarizes the key themes and future directions emerging from the conference "Medicinal and Crop Protection Chemistry: Breaking Barriers, Building Synergies," held in Como, Italy, in October 2025. The meeting highlighted the strong conceptual and technological convergence between medicinal and crop protection science, two disciplin
papers.summary: This perspective article summarizes key themes from a 2025 conference on the convergence of medicinal chemistry and crop protection science, framed within the WHO's 'One Health' perspective. It highlights shared conceptual and technological approaches between the two disciplines as a strategy to address global challenges in human, animal, and environmental health.

papers.title: Ligand‑Based Virtual Screening Discovery of Thienopyrimidinone Derivatives as Allosteric nSMase2 Modulators and Antivirals Against West Nile Virus.
papers.abstract: Orthoflaviviruses such as West Nile virus (WNV), Zika virus (ZIKV), or dengue virus (DENV) represent a growing global health threat, with millions of annual infections and no approved antiviral therapies. Targeting host pathways represents an alternative antiviral strategy that may overcome limitations associated with direct-acting antivirals, including resistance and narrow antiviral spectra. Neutral sphingomyelinase-2 (nSMase2) plays a central role in sphingolipid metabolism and has emerged as a host factor involved in the replication of several flaviviruses including WNV and ZIKV. Herein, w
papers.summary: This study used ligand-based virtual screening to identify thienopyrimidinone derivatives that act as allosteric modulators of nSMase2, a host enzyme involved in flavivirus replication. The compounds showed antiviral activity against West Nile virus, offering a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy against flaviviruses.

papers.title: Evaluating the outputs of ARAE-based molecular generative model for synthetic accessibility and BTK inhibition.
papers.abstract: The application of artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies in drug discovery represents a rapidly expanding area of interest, providing a valuable means for exploring uncharted chemical spaces to identify novel therapeutic candidates. In this proof-of-concept study, we evaluated hypothetical drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) architecture, which were not documented in existing chemical literature and databases, for their synthetic tractability and inhibitory effects on Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK). Utilizing a structure-based computational appro
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluates novel drug-like molecules generated by an adversarial regularized autoencoder (ARAE) for their synthetic accessibility and potential to inhibit Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK), using structure-based computational methods. The work demonstrates the utility of AI-based generative models in exploring uncharted chemical space for therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Computational design and evaluation of tacrine-based carbamate derivatives as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease is marked by a gradual decline in cognitive function accompanied by alterations in cholinergic signaling. Cholinergic function can be improved by targeting acetylcholinesterase (AChE). In this work, an in silico approach was applied to study a series of tacrine-based carbamate derivatives. 3D-QSAR models determined by CoMFA and CoMSIA and validated by cross-validation, external testing and Y-randomization were developed using a dataset of 27 compounds. A complementary 2D-QSAR model provided consistent results to support the proposed structure-activity relationships. The sta
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods, including 3D-QSAR (CoMFA/CoMSIA) and 2D-QSAR, to design and evaluate tacrine-based carbamate derivatives as potential acetylcholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's disease. The models were validated and provide structure-activity relationships that could guide the development of new drug candidates.

papers.title: Identification of a novel small-molecule modulator targeting SNX10 to inhibit osteoclastic bone resorption.
papers.abstract: Current antiresorptive therapies reduce bone loss by eliminating osteoclasts or inhibiting their formation. However, these approaches could disrupt osteoclast-osteoblast communication and cause serious complications with long-term usage. There is a need for developing new therapies that selectively inhibit resorptive function, while preserving osteoclast-mediated coupling effects to osteoblasts. Sorting nexin 10 (SNX10), an autosomal recessive osteopetrosis (ARO)-associated gene, plays a role mainly in osteoclast bone resorptive function. However, its potential as a target for developing thera
papers.journal: Journal of bone and mineral research : the official journal of the American Society for Bone and Mineral Research
papers.summary: This study identifies a novel small-molecule modulator that targets SNX10 to inhibit osteoclastic bone resorption, offering a potential therapeutic strategy that preserves osteoclast-osteoblast communication. The approach may overcome limitations of current antiresorptive therapies that disrupt this coupling and cause long-term complications.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review examines recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges: cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across modalities. It discusses emerging AI paradigms that address these barriers and their potential for clinical translation in drug development and precision therapy.

papers.title: GRASSP: RNA Language Model-Enhanced Graph Attention with Adaptive Gating for RNA-Small Molecule Binding Site Prediction.
papers.abstract: RNA-small molecule binding site prediction is crucial for targeted drug discovery. Sequence-based methods are efficient but often fail to capture structural dependencies between nucleotides, whereas structure-aware graph models can better represent spatial interactions but typically rely on complex structural annotations and multi-stage preprocessing pipelines. We therefore developed GRASSP, a streamlined hybrid deep learning framework that integrates pretrained RNA language model (LM) representations with adaptive graph refinement.
papers.summary: GRASSP is a new deep learning tool that predicts RNA-small molecule binding sites by combining RNA language model embeddings with graph attention and adaptive gating. It avoids complex structural preprocessing while still capturing spatial dependencies, offering a streamlined and efficient approach for targeted drug discovery.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, biological evaluation, and in silico studies of novel pyrrolidine based hybrids bearing indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea pharmacophores as multitarget hCA and AChE inhibitors.
papers.abstract: In this study, novel pyrrolidine-based compounds bearing indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea pharmacophores were rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase I/II (hCA I, hCA II) and acetylcholinesterase (AChE). The target compounds were synthesized via imine azomethine ylide 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition and in selected cases, benzoyl isothiocyanate condensation reactions. Their structures were fully characterized using FTIR, NMR, microanalysis, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction (for 1ba). Compound 2ad (hCA I, Ki = 35.56 ± 5.10 nM, hCA II, Ki = 31.
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrrolidine-based hybrid compounds incorporating indole, chromone, and benzoylthiourea groups, which act as dual inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase I/II and acetylcholinesterase. The most potent compound (2ad) showed nanomolar inhibition against hCA I and hCA II, with structures confirmed by X-ray crystallography and supported by in silico studies. This work provides a promising scaffold for developing multitarget therapeutics for conditions like Alzheimer's disease and glaucoma.

papers.title: LMF-CP: An Interpretable Multimodal Late-Fusion Framework for Compound Carcinogenicity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting the carcinogenicity of compounds is of great significance for drug discovery, clinical drug safety, and chemical risk assessment. Traditional methods for assessing carcinogenicity rely on animal testing, which suffers from limitations such as time-consuming processes, high costs, significant interspecies differences, and low predictive throughput. In recent years, computational modeling-based prediction methods (such as Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationships, QSAR) have made some progress, but they still face challenges such as insufficient molecular feature inform
papers.summary: This paper introduces LMF-CP, an interpretable multimodal late-fusion framework that predicts compound carcinogenicity by integrating multiple molecular data types, aiming to improve accuracy over traditional QSAR methods and reduce reliance on slow, costly animal testing. The framework emphasizes interpretability, which is important for drug safety and chemical risk assessment.

papers.title: Beyond the Score: Fixed-Budget Benchmarking of Virtual Screening Integration Strategies for Decision-Centric Drug Discovery.
papers.abstract: Virtual screening (VS) workflows often combine structure- and ligand-based methods; however, their value depends on the number of compounds that can be tested. We benchmarked 20 fixed-budget strategies derived from molecular docking (GNINA CNN score), maximum common substructure (MCS) similarity, and a calibrated machine-learning (ML)-QSAR classifier across five pharmacologically diverse targets. Individual methods, best-rank and worst-rank fusion, mean-rank consensus, and sequential funnels were evaluated at 1%, 5%, and 10% library fractions, with every strategy selecting the same number of c
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 20 virtual screening strategies that combine docking, ligand similarity, and machine-learning scoring under fixed experimental budgets across five drug targets. It finds that integration strategies outperform individual methods, with best-rank fusion and sequential funnels showing strong early enrichment, providing practical guidance for decision-centric drug discovery.

papers.title: Rational Design of Novel Thiazole-Clubbed Pyrimidine-Linked Hydrazone Conjugates as Promising RSK4 Inhibitors for Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Molecular Dynamics Simulations and In Vitro Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Background: Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains highly aggressive and continues to limit clinical treatment for substantial cancer-associated morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite advances in therapeutic interventions the lack of effective molecularly targeted treatments continues to restrict clinical management beyond conventional chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Among these therapeutic targets the ribosomal S6 kinase 4 (RSK4) has gained considerable attention because of its critical involvement in ESCC progression, survival and proliferation, suggesting its potential as a po
papers.summary: This study reports the rational design of novel thiazole-clubbed pyrimidine-linked hydrazone conjugates as potential inhibitors of RSK4 kinase for treating esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC). Using molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro evaluation, the authors identified promising lead compounds that may serve as a basis for targeted therapy against this aggressive cancer.

papers.title: An Integrated Computational Workflow for Discovering Alkaloid-Derived Ligands of Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 2.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2) is a key regulator of cell-cycle progression and a potential anticancer target. This study aimed to identify alkaloid-derived CDK2 ligands using an integrated computational workflow and to obtain preliminary evidence of their effects on cancer-cell viability. Methods: Molecular docking with mVina and fast pulling of ligand (FPL) simulations were benchmarked using 20 experimentally characterized CDK2 inhibitors. A library of 2692 PubChem-derived alkaloids was screened, followed by ADMET evaluation, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, an
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational workflow combining molecular docking, fast pulling of ligand simulations, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics to screen 2692 alkaloids for CDK2 inhibitors, a potential anticancer target. The workflow was benchmarked against known inhibitors and identified promising alkaloid-derived ligands with preliminary evidence of cancer-cell viability effects.

papers.title: Telmisartan Repurposing Targets Novel Biomarkers for Precision Colorectal Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality worldwide. The current therapeutic interventions are heavily constrained by the development of resistance and severe systemic toxicity. To address these challenges, this study integrated a multi-disciplinary framework involving high-throughput in silico screening followed by in vitro experimental validation to identify novel genetic targets of CRC and evaluate the efficacy of FDA-approved drugs. The primary objective was to identify safe and selective therapeutic agents capable of modulating t
papers.summary: This study uses a multi-disciplinary approach combining high-throughput computational screening with in vitro experiments to identify novel genetic targets for colorectal cancer (CRC) and repurpose the FDA-approved drug telmisartan as a potential therapy. The findings suggest telmisartan may modulate specific biomarkers relevant to CRC, offering a safer and more selective treatment option compared to current interventions.

papers.title: Multi-Target Neuroprotective Effects of Cordycepin and Adenosine from Cordyceps militaris Against Amyloid-β-Induced Neurotoxicity.
papers.abstract: Background:Cordyceps militaris (C. militaris) is a medicinal mushroom recognized for its diverse pharmacological activities, largely attributed to its principal bioactive nucleosides, cordycepin and adenosine. Although accumulating evidence supports their neuroprotective potential, the molecular mechanisms underlying their effects against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the neuroprotective effects of cordycepin and adenosine against amyloid-β (Aβ42)-induced neurotoxicity and explored their potential molecular mechanisms using integrated experime
papers.summary: This study investigates the neuroprotective effects of cordycepin and adenosine from Cordyceps militaris against amyloid-β-induced neurotoxicity in Alzheimer's disease models. Using integrated experimental approaches, the authors identify multi-target mechanisms that may underlie the protective actions of these compounds, offering potential therapeutic insights for AD.

papers.title: An Integrated Consensus Machine Learning and Structure-Based Workflow for the Discovery of Novel Tankyrase 1 Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Background: Tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) is a poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase involved in Wnt/β-catenin signaling, telomere maintenance, and genomic stability, making it an attractive therapeutic target in oncology. This study aimed to develop and apply an integrated computational workflow to identify novel TNKS1 inhibitor candidates. Methods: A curated dataset of experimentally validated TNKS1 inhibitors and property-matched DUD-E decoys was used to develop a consensus supervised machine learning (ML) model prioritization framework for ligand-based virtual screening, integrating Morgan fingerprints with t
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational workflow combining consensus machine learning with structure-based methods to discover novel Tankyrase 1 (TNKS1) inhibitors, a promising oncology target. The approach uses curated inhibitor datasets and decoys to build a ligand-based virtual screening framework, successfully identifying new candidate compounds.

papers.title: MetabolEx: Platform for Small-Molecule Metabolites Generation and Metabolic Pathway Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate metabolite prediction is essential for identifying safety liabilities and optimizing pharmacokinetic properties during early drug discovery. However, predicting metabolic fate remains a major bottleneck due to the risk of unexpected toxicity and drug-drug interactions. We present MetabolEx, a platform that integrates rule-based generation with machine learning prioritization to predict Phase I and II metabolism. MetabolEx utilizes 194 manually curated reactions in SMIRKS notation and machine learning classifiers trained on 41,041 substrate-metabolite pairs from multiple sources. This
papers.summary: MetabolEx is a new platform that combines rule-based reaction rules with machine learning to predict Phase I and II drug metabolism, addressing a key bottleneck in early drug discovery. It uses 194 curated reactions and classifiers trained on over 41,000 substrate-metabolite pairs to generate and prioritize potential metabolites, which could help identify safety liabilities and drug-drug interactions earlier.

papers.title: Integrated Virtual Screening and Molecular Electrostatic Surface Potential Descriptors for Predicting BACE1 Inhibitor Interactions in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Developing brain-penetrant BACE1 inhibitors remains a major challenge in Alzheimer's disease. Unlike conventional studies focusing solely on binding affinity, this work presents an integrated computational pipeline that prioritizes both potency and pharmacokinetic developability from the outset. A robust quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) model was built for 41 N-(pyridin-3-yl)-picolinamide derivatives using Molecular Electrostatic Surface Potential (MESP) descriptors. Principal component analysis identified three key electrostatic features - mean MESP, variance of negative ME
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline that combines QSAR modeling with molecular electrostatic surface potential (MESP) descriptors to predict BACE1 inhibitor interactions, prioritizing both potency and brain penetrability for Alzheimer's disease drug development. The model, built on 41 N-(pyridin-3-yl)-picolinamide derivatives, identifies key electrostatic features that could guide the design of more developable BACE1 inhibitors.

papers.title: Evaluating the Incremental Value of Three-Dimensional Conformer Descriptors for Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Prediction Using the B3DB Benchmark Dataset.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability remains a major challenge in central nervous system (CNS) drug discovery. Three-dimensional (3D) conformer-derived molecular descriptors are often proposed as improvements over conventional two-dimensional (2D) topological representations; however, their incremental predictive value remains unclear. Methods: Here, we systematically evaluated six molecular feature sets comprising curated 2D Mordred descriptors, Morgan/ECFP4 fingerprints, 3D conformer-derived descriptors, and their combinations, using LightGBM regression on
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates whether adding 3D conformer-derived molecular descriptors improves blood-brain barrier permeability prediction compared to standard 2D descriptors, using the B3DB benchmark dataset and LightGBM regression. The findings clarify the incremental predictive value of 3D descriptors for CNS drug discovery.

papers.title: RingKin: portraying the vast macrocyclic chemical universe surrounding kinase drugs.
papers.abstract: Cyclization strategies have emerged as a compelling approach to overcome persistent challenges in kinase drug development, notably poor selectivity and unfavorable pharmacological properties. Existing studies remain limited to individual kinases or retrospective analyses, while systematic exploration of the potentially vast and underexplored macrocyclic space for kinase modulation is still lacking. By leveraging artificial intelligence-based methods, we pioneered the creation of RingKin, an immense chemical universe encompassing 72.27 million macrocycles generated from 495 approved or clinical
papers.summary: RingKin is a new AI-generated chemical library of 72.27 million macrocycles derived from 495 approved or clinical kinase drugs, designed to systematically explore the vast underexplored macrocyclic space for kinase modulation. This resource could help overcome selectivity and pharmacological challenges in kinase drug development by providing a large, searchable universe of potential macrocyclic kinase inhibitors.

papers.title: Emerging therapies against infections due to free-living amoebae.
papers.abstract: Pathogenic free-living amoebae, including Naegleria fowleri, Acanthamoeba spp. and Balamuthia mandrillaris, are rare but frequently fatal opportunistic pathogens associated with severe central nervous system and ocular infections, and cutaneous infections. Despite advances in understanding their biology and pathogenesis, therapeutic options remain limited, mortality rates remain high, and delayed diagnosis continues to compromise clinical outcomes and public health responses.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the current state of therapies for infections caused by pathogenic free-living amoebae, which are rare but often fatal. It highlights that treatment options remain limited and mortality is high, underscoring the need for new therapeutic strategies and improved diagnosis.

papers.title: Hybrid artificial intelligence and quantum annealing as an optimization layer in drug discovery.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has greatly expanded the generative capacity of drug discovery, yet the ability to translate large candidate pools into structured, resource-aware decisions remains limited. This review addresses this emerging optimization bottleneck by examining quantum annealing as a potential decision-optimization layer within hybrid computational workflows. We focus on discrete, constraint-dominated tasks-such as compound subset selection, combinatorial design, and multi-objective prioritization-that can be formulated as quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) proble
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of quantum annealing as an optimization layer in hybrid AI workflows for drug discovery, focusing on discrete tasks like compound selection and multi-objective prioritization that can be formulated as QUBO problems. It highlights how quantum annealing can address the bottleneck of translating large candidate pools into resource-aware decisions.

papers.title: Antioxidant and Antidiabetic Activity of the Bulb Extract of Crinum amoenum Roxb. ex Ker Gawl: An Integrated In Vitro, In Vivo and In Silico Approach.
papers.abstract: Crinum amoenum Roxb. ex Ker Gawl. (C. amoenum) is traditionally used in Nepal, but its antidiabetic potential remains insufficiently validated. This study characterized the 80% (v/v) ethanol bulb extract of C. amoenum and evaluated its antioxidant, α-amylase inhibitory, hypoglycemic, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and ADMET profiles. The ethanolic bulb extract was evaluated through phytochemical screening, thin-layer chromatography, total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC) estimation, LC-MS analysis, antioxidant assays, α-amylase inhibition assays, ac
papers.summary: This study validates the traditional antidiabetic use of Crinum amoenum bulb extract by showing it has antioxidant and α-amylase inhibitory activity in vitro, hypoglycemic effects in vivo, and identifies bioactive compounds via LC-MS and in silico docking/MD simulations. The findings support further investigation of this plant as a natural source for diabetes management.

papers.title: Structural Preferences and ADMET Regulation of Fluorinated Small-Molecule Drugs.
papers.abstract: Fluorination is a powerful yet highly context-dependent strategy in medicinal chemistry. The F-DrugDatabase comprising 1,789 fluorinated small molecules was constructed, including 430 FDA-approved or marketed drugs. Using Bemis-Murcko scaffold analysis and a matched molecular pair (MMP) "defluorination-hydrogenation" approach, we reveal that 87.7% of fluorinated drugs contain only 1-3 fluorine atoms, with benzene scaffolds dominating (63.5%). Quantitative MMP analysis indicated that the -CF3 group was associated with an increase in predicted elimination half-life (average Δt1/2 = +12.24 h, P <
papers.summary: This study introduces the F-DrugDatabase of 1,789 fluorinated small molecules, including 430 approved drugs, and uses scaffold and matched molecular pair analyses to reveal that most fluorinated drugs contain 1-3 fluorine atoms on benzene rings. The -CF3 group is associated with increased predicted elimination half-life, highlighting how fluorination patterns influence drug metabolism and pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.title: GAMT-GINE: A Graph Isomorphism Network Integrating Continuous Spatial Awareness and Multi-Task Learning for Protein-Ligand Binding Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand interactions (PLIs) play a crucial role in drug discovery, and accurately predicting protein-ligand binding affinity (PLA) remains a central challenge in computer-aided drug design. Although graph neural networks (GNNs) have demonstrated considerable potential in molecular modeling, existing methods still face several limitations, including excessive reliance on hand-crafted chemical features, loss of spatial information, and difficulties in integrating heterogeneous affinity labels, which restrict their generalization capability in PLA prediction. To address these challenges, w
papers.summary: This paper introduces GAMT-GINE, a graph isomorphism network that integrates continuous spatial awareness and multi-task learning to improve protein-ligand binding affinity prediction. The method addresses limitations of existing graph neural networks by reducing reliance on hand-crafted features and better incorporating spatial information, potentially enhancing generalization in drug discovery applications.

papers.title: Combining Triazole Scaffold Repurposing and Generative Transformer Architecture for Structure-Based Inhibitor Design Targeting the LasR Quorum Sensing Receptor of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
papers.abstract: Background: The rapid escalation of multidrug-resistant P. aeruginosa necessitates anti-virulence strategies targeting quorum sensing rather than bacterial survival; however, integrating scaffold repurposing with generative AI to inhibit LasR remains underexplored. Here, we address this gap by combining triazole scaffold mining with transformer-based de novo molecular generation to systematically identify putative LasR inhibitors. Methods: An integrated computational pipeline involving Structure-based inhibitor design using Generative Transformer Architecture, deep learning-assisted GNINA resc
papers.summary: This study combines triazole scaffold repurposing with a generative transformer architecture to design novel inhibitors of the LasR quorum sensing receptor in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, an anti-virulence strategy against multidrug-resistant infections. The integrated computational pipeline, including deep learning-assisted docking rescoring, identified putative LasR inhibitors, demonstrating the potential of combining scaffold mining with generative AI for structure-based drug design.

papers.title: A Comparative Evaluation Framework Integrating Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models with ADME-Based Pharmacokinetic Assessment for HIV-Related Compounds.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Predicting the bioactivity of HIV-related compounds is essential for early-stage drug discovery. However, most existing machine learning (ML) studies emphasize predictive performance while overlooking the predicted pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness properties of prioritized compounds. This study presents a comparative framework integrating classical ML, deep learning, graph-based models, and complementary ADME-based pharmacokinetic assessment. Methods: Twelve predictive models were evaluated using stratified five-fold cross-validation on the MoleculeNet HIV dataset under
papers.summary: This study presents a comparative framework that integrates classical machine learning, deep learning, and graph-based models with ADME-based pharmacokinetic assessment to predict the bioactivity of HIV-related compounds. The authors evaluated twelve predictive models using stratified five-fold cross-validation on the MoleculeNet HIV dataset, highlighting the importance of considering pharmacokinetic properties alongside predictive performance in early-stage drug discovery.

papers.title: A Computational Framework for the Design and Development of Isoform Selective PI3Kα Inhibitors as Novel Anticancer Agents.
papers.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) is a promising anticancer drug target, and selective PI3Kα inhibition may provide both efficacy and an improved safety profile. This study aimed to design new potentially selective PI3Kα inhibitors using computer-aided drug design (CADD).
papers.summary: This study uses computer-aided drug design to develop new inhibitors that selectively target the PI3Kα isoform, a promising anticancer drug target. The computational framework aims to improve efficacy and safety by achieving isoform selectivity.

papers.title: Computational Investigation of Cinnamon Phytochemicals Targeting Key Cancer Signaling Pathways: Molecular Docking, ADMET and Molecular Dynamics Simulations Analysis.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains one of the leading causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for safe and effective therapeutic strategies targeting multiple oncogenic pathways. Cinnamon (Cinnamomum spp.) contains several bioactive phytochemicals with reported antioxidant and anticancer properties; however, their potential interactions with key cancer-associated signaling proteins have not been comprehensively investigated. In this study, an integrated computational and preliminary experimental approach was employed to evaluate four major cinnamon phytochemicals, namely e-cinnamaldehyd
papers.summary: This study computationally evaluates four cinnamon phytochemicals (including e-cinnamaldehyde) for their potential to target key cancer signaling pathways using molecular docking, ADMET prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations. The findings suggest these compounds may interact with multiple oncogenic proteins, providing a basis for further experimental validation in cancer therapy.

papers.title: Design and Synthesis of Novel Morpholine-Derived Nitrogen-Rich Scaffolds as Multifunctional Anticancer and Antibacterial Agents: Biological Evaluation and Computational Studies.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: The development of multifunctional small molecules capable of simultaneously addressing cancer progression and antimicrobial resistance represents an important challenge in medicinal chemistry. This study aimed to design, synthesize, and biologically evaluate a series of novel morpholine-based nitrogen-rich heterocyclic hybrids as potential anticancer and antibacterial agents, supported by computational investigations. Methods: Twelve morpholine-derived nitrogen-enriched heterocyclic hybrids incorporating pyran, triazine, pyrimidinone, and sulfur-containing scaffolds wer
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of twelve novel morpholine-derived nitrogen-rich heterocyclic hybrids with potential anticancer and antibacterial activities, supported by computational studies. The compounds were biologically evaluated, showing promising multifunctional activity against cancer cells and bacteria, highlighting their potential as leads for dual-action therapeutics.

papers.title: From Descriptor Learning to Binding Stability: An Explainable Machine Learning Pipeline for EGFR Double-Mutant Inhibitor Discovery.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance arising during cancer development and progression remains a major challenge in the treatment of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-driven tumors, particularly those harboring the clinically relevant T790M/L858R double mutation. In this study, we developed an integrated computational workflow combining explainable machine learning, virtual screening, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding free-energy calculations to identify novel inhibitors of this drug-resistant EGFR variant. An XGBoost regression model was trained using scaffold-aware cross-validation, Bayesian hype
papers.summary: This study presents an integrated computational pipeline combining explainable machine learning, virtual screening, molecular dynamics, and binding free-energy calculations to identify novel inhibitors of the drug-resistant EGFR T790M/L858R double mutant. The approach demonstrates a practical workflow for discovering compounds that may overcome resistance in EGFR-driven cancers.

papers.title: ERβ-Score: An Interpretable Machine Learning-Based Scoring Function and Web Server for Estrogen Receptor β-Guided Drug Discovery in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is the most clinically aggressive subtype of breast cancer, characterized by the absence of targetable hormone receptors and HER2 amplification, significantly constraining treatment choices. Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) has emerged as a biologically relevant yet underutilized target in TNBC, with its re-expression linked to tumor suppression and improved prognosis, prompting the development of selective ERβ modulators as a precision therapeutic approach. We introduce ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning scoring system developed using a curated datas
papers.summary: The authors developed ERβ-Score, an interpretable machine learning-based scoring function and web server to support drug discovery targeting Estrogen Receptor Beta (ERβ) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). The tool aims to identify selective ERβ modulators, leveraging ERβ's tumor-suppressive role in this aggressive cancer subtype.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics Identification of Baicalein as a Phytochemical Inhibitor of CHEK1 in Serous Ovarian Cancer: A Multi-Stage In Silico Drug Discovery Approach.
papers.abstract: Background: Serous ovarian cancer (SOC) is the most aggressive subtype of epithelial ovarian cancer, frequently diagnosed at advanced stages with poor prognosis and chemotherapy resistance. Checkpoint kinase 1 (CHEK1), a key regulator of the DNA damage response, is overexpressed in ovarian cancer, making it a promising therapeutic target. No study has systematically evaluated natural compounds as CHEK1 inhibitors in SOC through an integrative transcriptomic and computational framework. Methods: A meta-analysis of three GEO datasets (GSE27651, GSE36668, GSE54388; n = 83) was performed using Ima
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative in silico approach—combining meta-analysis of ovarian cancer transcriptomic datasets with molecular docking and dynamics—to identify baicalein, a natural phytochemical, as a potential inhibitor of CHEK1, a key DNA damage response protein overexpressed in serous ovarian cancer. The findings suggest baicalein may serve as a lead compound for targeted therapy in this aggressive cancer subtype, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Natural-Product Aromatase (CYP19A1) Inhibitors via Integrated Molecular Docking and QSAR Modelling.
papers.abstract: Aromatase (CYP19A1) is the rate-limiting enzyme in estrogen biosynthesis and the principal therapeutic target for estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer. Despite the clinical success of third-generation aromatase inhibitors (AIs) such as letrozole and anastrozole, acquired resistance and systemic adverse effects, including musculoskeletal pain, bone density loss, and cardiovascular complications, which necessitate the identification of novel scaffolds. This study employs an integrated computational pipeline combining ligand-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) mode
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods, including QSAR modeling and molecular docking, to screen natural products for potential aromatase (CYP19A1) inhibitors, aiming to find new drug candidates for ER+ breast cancer that may overcome resistance and side effects of current treatments. The integrated pipeline identifies promising natural compounds that could serve as leads for further development.

papers.title: De Novo Molecular Design and Bioactivity Prediction of Novel Hexahydroquinolines as Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (CDPK4) Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum Calcium-Dependent Protein Kinase 4 (PfCDPK4) is a validated target for malaria transmission-blocking interventions, as its inhibition disrupts male gametocyte exflagellation. Hexahydroquinolines (HHQs) have emerged as promising gametocytocidal agents. This study aimed to design novel HHQs as potential PfCDPK4 inhibitors with good binding affinity, favourable pharmacokinetics, and structural stability. A library of 20,000 novel HHQ analogs was generated using genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design in AlvaBuilder and systematically filtered through a pipeline com
papers.summary: This study used genetic algorithm-driven de novo molecular design to generate 20,000 novel hexahydroquinoline analogs and filter them for potential inhibitors of Plasmodium falciparum CDPK4, a malaria transmission-blocking target. The pipeline prioritized compounds with good predicted binding affinity, pharmacokinetics, and structural stability, offering new candidates for antimalarial drug development.

papers.title: MetaCYP: a unified framework for prediction of cytochrome P450 metabolic sites and reaction types via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes are the predominant drug-metabolizing proteins in humans, collectively governing the structural transformation of drugs and xenobiotics while directly shaping their pharmacological activity and toxicological profiles. Accurate prediction of CYP-substrate reaction sites and reaction types is therefore central to drug discovery and metabolic risk assessment. Existing computational models, however, largely depend on intrinsic molecular properties or hardcoded reaction rules, constraining their generalization across CYP isoforms.
papers.summary: MetaCYP is a new multimodal deep learning framework that predicts both the metabolic sites and reaction types of cytochrome P450 enzymes on drug molecules, addressing limitations of existing models that rely on molecular properties or hardcoded rules. It improves generalization across different CYP isoforms, which is important for drug discovery and safety assessment.

papers.title: AI-enhanced virtual screening identifies a potent small-molecule modulator of ClC-3 for cervical cancer drug discovery.
papers.abstract: ClC-3 chloride channels play essential roles in cervical cancer progression by regulating lysosomal acidification, cell volume homeostasis, and chemoresistance. However, no highly selective small-molecule modulators of ClC-3 have been reported to date. Motivated by the urgent clinical need to reverse ClC-3-mediated chemoresistance and the challenge of processing massive chemical libraries under limited computational hardware resources, we propose a novel AI-driven Drug Discovery (AIDD) pipeline. Here, we present an integrated virtual drug discovery framework that transitions from traditional C
papers.summary: The authors developed an AI-driven virtual screening pipeline to identify the first potent small-molecule modulator of the ClC-3 chloride channel, which is implicated in cervical cancer progression and chemoresistance. This approach addresses the lack of selective ClC-3 inhibitors and demonstrates a computationally efficient strategy for drug discovery under limited hardware resources.

papers.title: NN-assisted image analysis for quantifying intracellular Trypanosoma cruzi infection.
papers.abstract: Quantification of intracellular Trypanosoma cruzi infection remains a central, yet methodologically challenging step in Chagas disease research and early-stage drug discovery. Current approaches largely rely on manual microscopy-based counting or on genetically modified parasites, both of which present limitations in scalability, reproducibility, or accessibility. Here, we developed and validated a neural network (NN)-based pipeline for the automated quantification of infection rates and parasite burden in mammalian cells using images stained exclusively with DNA-binding fluorescent dyes. Two
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This paper presents a neural network-based image analysis pipeline that automatically quantifies intracellular Trypanosoma cruzi infection in mammalian cells using only DNA-binding fluorescent stains, eliminating the need for genetically modified parasites. The approach offers a scalable and reproducible alternative to manual microscopy counting, which could facilitate Chagas disease research and drug discovery.

papers.title: Repositioning antiviral phytoconstituents as broad-spectrum inhibitors of influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein.
papers.abstract: Viral respiratory infections still exist as a major global health concern. Influenza A viruses and human metapneumoviruses are among the main pathogens responsible for infections that can progress to severe acute respiratory forms. Despite the availability of certain therapeutic options, the need for effective treatment remains an issue. The exploration of innovative approaches based on medicinal plants, capable of simultaneously targeting several viruses, represents a promising strategic option for limiting the viral activity of these pathogens. In this work, an integrated computational workf
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to screen antiviral phytoconstituents as potential broad-spectrum inhibitors against influenza A neuraminidase and human metapneumovirus fusion protein. The findings suggest that certain plant-derived compounds may serve as dual-target candidates for treating respiratory viral infections, though experimental validation is needed.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of DENV-1 Isolates From Pakistan Reveals Immunogenic Variability and Antiviral Potential of Phytochemicals Targeting the CprM Region.
papers.abstract: Dengue virus (DENV), a mosquito-borne arbovirus, remains a critical global health concern, causing approximately 390 million infections annually. Dengue fever poses significant challenges to healthcare systems in endemic regions like Pakistan due to the presence of four established serotypes (DENV-1-DENV-4) and the potential emergence of a fifth serotype (DENV-5). The current study aimed to investigate molecular characteristics of DENV-1 isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, focusing on serotyping, genetic variability in the CprM junction region, and identification of potential antiviral phytochem
papers.summary: This study characterizes DENV-1 isolates from Peshawar, Pakistan, by analyzing genetic variability in the CprM junction region and evaluating the immunogenic potential of the resulting variants. The authors also identify phytochemicals that may target this region as potential antiviral candidates, offering insights for vaccine and therapeutic development against dengue in endemic regions.

papers.title: Computational identification and evaluation of Adenium obesum phytochemicals as potential EGFR inhibitors for targeted therapy against non-small-cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of lung cancer-related mortality, largely driven by aberrant activation of the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). Despite the clinical success of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), intrinsic and acquired resistance, coupled with safety concerns, highlight the need for novel, safer inhibitors. Natural products represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse bioactive compounds with favorable biocompatibility. In this study, a comprehensive in silico approach is used to evaluate phytochemicals from Adenium obesum a
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to screen phytochemicals from Adenium obesum as potential inhibitors of EGFR for treating non-small-cell lung cancer. The authors identify promising natural compounds that may serve as leads for developing safer EGFR-targeted therapies, addressing the need for alternatives to current tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
